title: Pretreatment for pharmaceutical water systems | Aquemi
meta: Multimedia, softening, carbon and bisulfite pretreatment sized to Canadian municipal water, including chloramine removal and cold winter feed.
headline: Pretreatment
lead: Pretreatment protects your reverse osmosis (RO) membranes and stills from chlorine, chloramine, hardness and particles, so the purification stage downstream runs to its design life.

blocks.h: Start from the water you have
body: USP requires feed water for pharmaceutical water to meet drinking water standards such as those of the US EPA, and in Canada most sites draw municipal water that meets the Guidelines for Canadian Drinking Water Quality. Drinking water standards protect people, not membranes.

Many Canadian municipal supplies use chloramine as a secondary disinfectant, and it passes through softeners and attacks polyamide RO membranes. Spring runoff raises turbidity and organic load, and winter supply can fall to 2–5 °C. We design pretreatment from a year of your water data, not one sample.

rows.m: Online ORP or total chlorine analyser

blocks.caption: A break tank isolates the plant from the municipal supply. Multimedia filtration removes particles. Duplex softeners exchange calcium and magnesium for sodium. Activated carbon or sodium bisulfite dosing removes chlorine and chloramine. A 5 µm cartridge filter protects the RO pumps.

items.q: What water analysis do you need?
items.a: At minimum: hardness, alkalinity, total dissolved solids, silica, iron, manganese, total and free chlorine, TOC, turbidity and temperature. Seasonal data is better than one sample.

items.q: Our municipality switched to chloramine. What changes?
items.a: Standard carbon beds remove chloramine slowly. We check contact time, consider catalytic carbon or bisulfite, and verify at the RO inlet with an online analyser.

items.q: Is pretreatment part of the validated system?
items.a: Usually pretreatment is outside the GMP boundary but its performance affects the validated system. We document it and monitor its outlet to support your risk assessment.
